eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Ten
subtitle: Lesson 83 · Window and Ranking Functions

code:
SELECT OrderDate, TotalDue,
  LAG(TotalDue) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate)
    AS PreviousOrderTotalDue
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader;
caption: LAG() reaches back to the row BEFORE the current one.

code:
SELECT OrderDate, TotalDue,
  LEAD(TotalDue) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate)
    AS NextOrderTotalDue
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader;
caption: Same syntax, opposite direction — the row AFTER the current one.

code:
LAG(TotalDue, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate)
-- offset: how many rows back (default 1)
-- default: value used when no such row exists
caption: The first row has no previous row — default fills the gap.

code:
SELECT OrderDate, TotalDue,
  TotalDue - LAG(TotalDue) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate)
    AS ChangeFromPreviousOrder
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader;
caption: The classic use case: comparing each row to the one before it.
